document.title: Kidney
document.subtitle: Coronal section with the collecting system opened
document.description: A section through an idealised adult human kidney shows cortical tissue, medullary pyramids and the opened collecting system. Selected hilar vessels are retained.
document.caption: Illustrative coronal section. Calyces and renal pelvis are opened to show their continuity. Selected vessels only; not to scale.
document.reference_line: Anatomical reference: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 25.3.

document.title: Muscular artery
document.subtitle: Oblique section through the vessel wall
document.description: An oblique section through an idealised muscular artery distinguishes the outer supporting coat, muscular media, internal elastic lamina, intima and lumen. Sparse surface vessels are shown.
document.caption: Illustrative muscular artery. Wall thickness and layer proportions are exaggerated for visibility; not a quantitative histological section.
document.reference_line: Anatomical reference: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 20.1.

document.title: Kidney
document.subtitle: External surface and structures at the hilum
document.description: An idealised adult kidney has a convex lateral border, a concave medial hilum, a smooth capsular surface, renal artery, renal vein and ureter.
document.caption: External illustrative view. Hilar structures have been separated for clarity. No sided anatomical variation is implied; not to scale.
document.reference_line: Anatomical reference: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 25.3.

document.title: Peripheral nerve
document.subtitle: Oblique section showing fascicles and their envelopes
document.description: An idealised peripheral nerve in oblique section contains several fascicles within the epineurium. Each fascicle is bounded by perineurium and contains illustrated myelinated fibres and endoneurial supporting tissue.
document.caption: Illustrative nerve section. Fascicle and fibre counts are arbitrary; unmyelinated fibres are omitted. Not a quantitative histological section.
document.reference_line: Anatomical reference: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 13.4.

document.title: Selective detail inside a cell
document.subtitle: Compartment relationships are preserved; relative sizes are explanatory
document.description: A generic nucleated cell is shown with a nucleus, mitochondria, rough endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus and a lysosome. Organelles are contained within the cell outline. Their numbers and relative dimensions are chosen for explanation rather than representing a measured cell.

claims.text: A generic nucleated cell is shown with a nucleus, mitochondria, rough endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus and a lysosome. Organelles are contained within the cell outline. Their numbers and relative dimensions are chosen for explanation rather than representing a measured cell.

document.caption: Schematic; not to scale. A generic cell, not a complete cell-type reconstruction. Organelle counts and positions are illustrative. Each selected structure remains individually editable.

templates.name: A signal is not a transported molecule

document.title: A signal is not a transported molecule
document.subtitle: House notation separates association, activation and inhibition
document.description: An intentionally hypothetical signalling example. A ligand associates with an extracellular receptor domain. The receptor is shown at a membrane boundary. A proposed intracellular activation leads to a generic effector, while a second proposed relation inhibits the effector. Dashed relationships are illustrative, not an asserted named pathway.

sources.title: OpenStax Biology 2e, Signalling Molecules and Receptors

claims.text: A ligand associates with the receptor in this explanatory example.
A receptor-associated signal activates an effector in this invented example.
A regulator inhibits the effector in this invented example.

document.caption: Illustrative mechanism only; not a named pathway or evidence of molecular binding. Dashed lines denote hypothetical relationships. Open arrow: activation. T-bar: inhibition. Plain line: association.

document.title: The epithelial barrier
document.subtitle: A continuous tissue section, from the lumen to the supporting tissue
document.description: An explanatory section of a polarised epithelial sheet. Its apical surface and microvilli are above the cell bodies; a goblet cell lies among columnar cells. Junctions lie between neighbouring cells, and a basement membrane separates the epithelial layer from the underlying connective tissue.

claims.text: An explanatory section of a polarised epithelial sheet. Its apical surface and microvilli are above the cell bodies; a goblet cell lies among columnar cells. Junctions lie between neighbouring cells, and a basement membrane separates the epithelial layer from the underlying connective tissue.

document.caption: Schematic; not to scale. Cell number and dimensions are illustrative. Anatomy reference: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 4.2.

document.title: One tissue, three explanatory scales
document.subtitle: Zoom connectors indicate correspondence, not biological causation
document.description: A tissue section, a columnar cell symbol and a membrane-junction detail are displayed at different illustrative scales. The first zoom begins in the epithelial sheet and selects a columnar cell. The second selects the upper lateral interface and shows a generic junction between membranes. No magnification value is claimed.

claims.text: A tissue section, a columnar cell symbol and a membrane-junction detail are displayed at different illustrative scales. The first zoom begins in the epithelial sheet and selects a columnar cell. The second selects the upper lateral interface and shows a generic junction between membranes. No magnification value is claimed.

labels.text: The cell within a continuous epithelial sheet
Neighbouring membranes with a junctional symbol

document.caption: Schematic at unequal, uncalibrated scales. Dashed connectors mean a change of scale, not transport or causation. Junction detail is symbolic, not a molecular reconstruction.

templates.name: A matched view preserves the comparison

document.title: A matched view preserves the comparison
document.subtitle: The same tissue geometry, shown at the same scale, supports two reading tasks
document.description: Two identical epithelial sections are displayed at a shared scale. The left annotation identifies cellular organisation; the right identifies the basal interface. Only the annotation changes. The figure does not depict disease, treatment, before-and-after improvement or measured clinical data.

claims.text: Two identical epithelial sections are displayed at a shared scale. The left annotation identifies cellular organisation; the right identifies the basal interface. Only the annotation changes. The figure does not depict disease, treatment, before-and-after improvement or measured clinical data.

document.caption: Matched explanatory views; not patient observations. Geometry, orientation and magnification are fixed. Only the selected label changes; no disease or treatment effect is implied.

document.title: Continuity of the nephron
document.subtitle: The tubular route is unfolded to make its connections legible
document.description: A simplified nephron map shows a renal corpuscle leading to a proximal tubule, a descending limb, the nephron loop, an ascending limb and a distal tubule. The distal route drains into an associated collecting duct. Cortex and medulla are indicated; vascular branches are omitted.

sources.title: OpenStax A&P 2e, Chapter 25 review / microscopic anatomy

claims.text: A simplified nephron map shows a renal corpuscle leading to a proximal tubule, a descending limb, the nephron loop, an ascending limb and a distal tubule. The distal route drains into an associated collecting duct. Cortex and medulla are indicated; vascular branches are omitted.

document.caption: Unfolded schematic; not to scale. The collecting duct is associated drainage, not part of the nephron. Blood vessels and the filtration barrier are omitted.

document.title: From a specimen to an interpretable image
document.subtitle: A descriptive workflow, without fabricated experimental results
document.description: A conceptual research workflow progresses from a labelled sample vial to a prepared microscope slide, then to optical microscopy. The arrows indicate the order of activities, not a biological mechanism. No sample results, operating instructions, measurements or patient identifiers are shown.

labels.text: A defined material and an explicit identity
Preparation is described in the study methods
Observed data remain separate from illustration

document.caption: Conceptual workflow; not an operating protocol. Sequence arrows indicate stages of work, not causal biological effects. No microscopy result or sample measurement is fabricated.

document.title: A muscular artery in section
document.subtitle: The wall is organised into layers around a continuous lumen
document.description: A transverse explanatory view of a generic muscular artery. Labels identify the lumen, the tunica intima, the tunica media and the tunica externa or adventitia. The repeated elongated marks in the media symbolise circumferential smooth muscle, not measured cell counts.

claims.text: A transverse explanatory view of a generic muscular artery. Labels identify the lumen, the tunica intima, the tunica media and the tunica externa or adventitia. The repeated elongated marks in the media symbolise circumferential smooth muscle, not measured cell counts.

document.caption: Schematic; not to scale. Layer widths are explanatory, not measured. The outer layer is the tunica externa (adventitia). Reference: OpenStax, A&P 2e, section 20.1.
